AgentCreate.description:
The body of `POST /agents`: an agent of your team or of your own.

The agent declares what it IS (instructions, an optional plugin agent, MCP servers, limits, the
credentials it needs). The PLATFORM decides what it runs on: the image, the model and the harness
are your tenant's free-prompt runtime, and the network it reaches never goes beyond your tenant's
policy. An agent needs at least `instructions` or a `plugin_agent`.

egress.description: Narrows the network the agent reaches. Omit it to inherit everything your tenant's policy grants a free prompt; send it to keep only these destinations (plus the model gateway and the object store the run needs). A destination beyond the policy is `422 agent_egress_not_allowed`: it can never widen it.
egress.title: Egress

env_credentials.description: Credentials the agent receives as ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES of its container: `{VARIABLE: credential}`. `VARIABLE` is `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` and not one the runtime uses (`ANTHROPIC_*`, `AGENT_*`, `MCP_*`, `CLAUDE_*`, `PATH`, `HOME`, ... : `422 env_var_invalid`). A `team` agent names credentials of the team as `shared:<name>` (`GET /credentials?scope=shared`); a `personal` agent names its owner's own. A credential that does not exist, or that the agent cannot use, is `422 credential_unavailable` or `422 shared_credential_not_allowed`. The value never appears in the task, the API or the published logs, but the agent can print it: use credentials with the least permission that does the job.

The farm resolves the tag to its digest and reads those labels when it accepts each task (`422 image_not_found`, `422 registry_auth_required`, `422 image_labels_invalid`, `503 registry_unavailable`). A task can send its own.

CallbackIn.description:
Where to announce that the task ended: a signed `POST` once it is terminal.

The body is `{task_id, state, failure_reason, finished_at, correlation_id}`, never the result
(fetch it with `GET /tasks/{task_id}/result`). The farm signs it with its own Ed25519 key:
`X-Agent-Farm-Signature-Ed25519` is the base64 signature of `"<X-Agent-Farm-Timestamp>.<raw body>"`,
`X-Agent-Farm-Key-Id` says which key of `GET /callback-key` verifies it. Retried with a growing
wait (5 attempts over about 15 minutes) on a network error, `408`, `429` or `5xx`; a redirect is
not followed. Delivery is at least once: deduplicate by `task_id`.

McpServerIn.description:
A remote MCP server (HTTP) the agent can use during this task. The secret never travels in the
task: it is one of YOUR credentials, named here.

Two forms, told apart by whether `url` is present:

- **The credential is the address** (no `url`): for servers whose URL carries the key in its path,
  such as `https://portal.example.com/mcp/<key>`. Register the whole URL as a credential of type
  `mcp_url`. The URL is then never in the task, the API, the logs or the result.
- **A public address and a token** (`url` present): register the token as a credential of type
  `mcp_token`. It is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or as the header named in `header`.

**Servers of the house.** The deployment can offer some by name (see the deployment's documentation). With no
`url` and one of those names, the server is the house's: its address and header are fixed, the
credential is an `mcp_token` and `header` must be omitted. Those names are reserved: an `mcp_url`
credential under one of them is refused (`422 mcp_credential_type_mismatch`).

credential.description: Name of one of YOUR credentials (`GET /credentials`): type `mcp_url` when `url` is omitted, `mcp_token` when it is sent. A name, never the secret itself. A team agent (`POST /agents`, `scope: team`) names a credential of the team as `shared:<name>` (`GET /credentials?scope=shared`), and has to when it sends a `url`.
credential.title: Credential

header.description: Only with `url`. Header that carries the token. Default `Authorization`, sent as `Bearer <token>`; any other header carries the token as is.

name.title: Name

url.description: `https` address of the MCP server, WITHOUT any secret in it (it is stored and returned as sent). Omit it when the credential is the whole address (`mcp_url`).
url.title: Url

info.description:
Control plane of the agent farm: run an AI agent on a task, follow it, read its result and logs,
and schedule it to repeat. Everything here is scoped to the tenant and, within it, to the person
whose key is used.

**How to use it.** Authenticate every call with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Start with
`GET /whoami` (who you are, whether you are a tenant admin, when the key expires) and
`GET /agents` (what you can launch and what each agent needs). Launch with `POST /tasks`, poll
`GET /tasks/{task_id}` until `state` is terminal, then `GET /tasks/{task_id}/result`.

**Errors** always have the shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "details"}}`; branch on `code`, and repeat only when
`retryable` is true.
Each operation lists the codes it can return. Someone else's resource is `404`, never `403`.

**Cost and safety.** Running a task spends model tokens and tenant capacity. What you put in a
`prompt` or `input` is stored by the farm and can reach logs: never put secrets in it, register
them with `POST /credentials` and refer to them by name.
info.title: Agent Farm — Farm API

The agent catalogue for your tenant. Read this before building a task so the request is not rejected. Read-only, free.

post.description:
Defines an agent you launch by its `slug` (`agent_id` in `POST /tasks`). It declares its `instructions` (they travel in front of the task's `input`: the agent reads them as the start of its task, not as a system prompt), an optional `plugin_agent`, its `mcp_servers`, default `limits` and the `credentials` it may be given. It can run on its own `image` (a public one that carries the farm's layer), with `services` next to it in its pod and a larger `/work` (`work_size`); the model and the harness are your tenant's free-prompt runtime, and its network never goes beyond your tenant's policy: `egress` can only narrow it.

`scope: team` is usable by everybody in the tenant and only a tenant admin (`farm:tenant:admin`) can create it (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise); `scope: personal` is yours alone. The slug cannot be one a platform agent or one of your team's already has (`409 agent_slug_taken`), so what you launch by name is never ambiguous.

A team agent's MCP servers and credentials are those of whoever launches it; a personal agent's are its owner's. **State change:** stores the definition; nothing runs and nothing is spent.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

post.description:
Stores a secret, such as a git token, so tasks can use it BY NAME (`workspace.credentials_ref`) without it ever appearing in a request. **Write-only:** no endpoint returns the value afterwards, only its metadata. Writing a `name` you already own **rotates** it (answer `200`); a new name answers `201`.

Names are yours: another person in the tenant can use the same name for their own secret. Prefer short-lived, narrowly scoped tokens: the farm is an alpha and secrets are stored in plain form on its side.

With `scope: shared` the credential belongs to the whole team: only a tenant admin (`farm:tenant:admin`) can write, rotate or delete it (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise), the name is unique in the tenant, and the team's agents declare it as `shared:<name>` (`env_credentials`, `mcp_servers`). Everybody in the tenant can list its name and fingerprint; nobody can read its value.

Never log or echo the `value` you send.

**Needs scope:** `farm:credentials:write`.

post.description:
Runs the same task again and again on a cron expression, without anyone re-sending the request. `task` is exactly a `POST /tasks` body and is validated now, with the same errors, so a schedule that could never run is refused up front; it is validated again on every firing.

**Cost:** each firing is a real task that spends model tokens, so a frequent cron adds up. Count the firings before creating one. The tenant has a cap on schedules (`429 quota_exceeded`).

**Behaviour:** the cron is evaluated in `recurrence.timezone` (08:00 stays 08:00 across DST). If the farm was down, at most ONE catch-up firing happens and the rest are counted in `missed_runs`. A firing never depends on your key still being valid. A fired task belongs to the schedule's owner and has `origin: schedule`.

**State change:** creates the schedule `active` (or `finished` if its first occurrence is already past `ends_at`).

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

get.description:
Lists your tasks (a tenant admin sees everyone's; add `owner=me` to see only their own). Newest first (unless `updated_since`, below), in pages: when `next_cursor` is not null, pass it as `cursor` for the next page. All filters combine with AND. `state` takes one state or several separated by commas (`state=queued,running`).

**Following changes:** pass `updated_since`. The order is then oldest change first, by `updated_at` (ties by task), and `next_cursor` continues in that order; follow it until it is null. A task that changes while you page comes out again later in the same round, with its new `updated_at`. For the next round ask for `updated_since = <greatest updated_at seen> - 30 s` (a write stamped just before that instant can become visible a little later) and drop what you already have by `(task_id, updated_at)`. A cursor from one kind of listing is a `422` in the other.

Read-only, free. Each item is the full task, except that `queue_position` is only on `GET /tasks/{task_id}`. For a tenant admin each task also carries `owner`.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:read`.

post.description:
Starts a new task. Send exactly one of `agent_id` (a catalogue agent, see `GET /agents`, plus its `input`) or `prompt` (free-form, only for tenants that allow it).

**Cost:** every task runs a model and consumes tenant capacity and model spend; it is not free to try out. Check `GET /agents` for what an agent needs (a `workspace`, a credential) before sending.

**State change:** creates the task in `pending`; the farm then queues and runs it. Nothing is returned about the outcome: poll `GET /tasks/{task_id}`, then fetch `GET /tasks/{task_id}/result` once the state is terminal.

**Idempotent:** the same `correlation_id` from the same person never creates a second task: the answer is `200` with the existing one (and, if it could not be dispatched the first time, the dispatch is retried). Use a new `correlation_id` for a genuinely new task.

**Callback:** with `callback`, the farm announces the end of the task with a `POST` signed by the farm (Ed25519, public key at `GET /callback-key`) to a public `https` address of yours; see `CallbackIn`.

**Never put secrets in `prompt` or `input`:** they are stored and can reach logs. Register secrets with `POST /credentials` and refer to them by name.

The `tenant` is never accepted in the body (`tenant_not_accepted`): it comes from your key.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

Stops a `pending`, `queued` or `running` task and marks it `cancelled`. **It cancels; it does not delete** the task or its data: they stay readable until retention removes them.

Changes state, so confirm with the person first if it is not clearly what they asked. A task that already finished answers `409 task_not_cancellable`. Work the agent had already done (and its model cost) is not undone.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:cancel`.

get.description:
The full task: its state, failure reason, limits, timings and usage so far. After `POST /tasks`, ask until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `expired`. While `queued`, `queue_position` says how many tasks are ahead.

Add `wait=<seconds>` (0 to 30) to make the call do the waiting: it answers as soon as the task is in a terminal state, or when the seconds run out with whatever state it has then. Above 30 is a `422`, never a shorter wait. Chain calls for longer waits.

A task launched with a `callback` carries `callback`: where it is sent and how its delivery is going (`status`, `attempts`, `last_error`).

Read-only, free. A task that is not yours answers `404`, the same as one that does not exist.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:read`.

get.description:
For a finished task, returns the result's `summary`, its usage and a presigned `result.url` to download the full JSON, whose shape is the `ResultDocument` schema (`task_id`, `state`, `result`, `usage`, `session_ref`, ...). The link works for about five minutes: fetch it right away, and call this again for a fresh one.

Only for terminal tasks. A task still running answers `409 task_not_terminal` (ask again later); one that failed or was cancelled before producing anything answers `409 task_has_no_result` (nothing to fetch, check `failure_reason` on the task instead). Reading a result is recorded in the audit trail. Free.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:read`.

get.description:
Describes the key used for this call: its `subject` (the owner of everything it creates), its `tenant`, the `scopes` it carries, whether it is a tenant admin, and when it expires. Nothing secret is returned (never the key itself).

Call it first in a session: it tells a client whether it may see other people's tasks (`is_admin`), how long the key has left and whether it can launch a free `prompt` (`free_prompt`; if false, use a catalogue `agent_id`). It changes nothing and costs nothing.

Any valid key can call it; no scope is needed.
